papers.title: Chiral edge modes from lattice Chern-Simons theory
papers.abstract: It is shown that a level $k$ Abelian lattice Chern-Simons theory with continuum time and a spatial square lattice, which is a topological field theory on the latticized plane and torus, when quantized on a spatial cylinder reduces to chiral edge excitations, exactly localized on the two boundaries and carrying two commuting lattice versions of the level-$k$ $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra of opposite chirality. The algebras are represented on a Fock space in the noncompact theory and by a finite Weyl algebra in the compact one. We also observe that the theory has a natural framing of Wilson loops which exhibits the correct framing anomaly.

papers.title: Stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter
papers.abstract: In quantum many-body physics and quantum field theory, it is often assumed that gapped systems remain gapped under sufficiently weak local perturbations. However, to what extent this assumption holds is elusive, except for some special systems. In this work, we examine the stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter that is only subject to two physically natural conditions, locality and translation invariance. We first show that in any spatial dimension, there are gapped local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap, i.e., they become gapless under certain arbitrarily weak local perturbation in the thermodynamic limit. We then prove that for both spin and fermionic systems in one dimension, such Hamiltonians with an unstable gap must not only break translation invariance but also be fine-tuned. We further show that in any dimension greater than one, there are fine-tuned local translation invariant Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap. These results greatly sharpen our understanding of the fundamental problem of the stability of quantum phases of matter. We also discuss implications of our results on, for example, anyon superconductivity and higher-form symmetries.

papers.title: Classification and Signatures of Dissipative Quantum Hall-Superconductor Junctions
papers.abstract:
Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) edges with proximity-induced superconductivity can host parafermionic zero modes (PZMs), making them a promising platform for topological quantum computing. Recent experiments [G"ul et al., Phys. Rev. X 12, 021057 (2022)] measured the edge conductance from crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) between counter-propagating FQH edges separated by a narrow superconductor. The observed conductance was small and non-quantized, with two distinct behaviors: some states show temperature-independent conductance, while others show conductance that grows as temperature decreases. We explain these results by dissipation to sub-gap modes in the superconductor and present a phase diagram for the FQH-superconductor junction. We show that for Jain states, temperature-independent non-quantized conductance occurs only in the presence of an integer mode (such as at filling $
u=1\pm rac{1}{m}$, with odd $m\geq3$) strongly coupled to the dissipative channel. The predicted temperature trends qualitatively agree with the experiment, which shows temperature-independent conductance for $
u=2/3$ and integer states, but not for $
u=1/3$ and $
u=2/5$. We propose comparing $
u=4/3$ and $2/3$ to test the predicted influence of the relative chirality of integer and fractional modes.

papers.title: Noise-Induced Topology in Chiral Quantum Walks
papers.abstract: Noise typically destroys quantum coherence and washes out transport phenomena that rely on interference. Chiral quantum walks are a case in point: a particle hopping on a lattice threaded by a magnetic flux can spread asymmetrically due to interference between paths, an asymmetry that noise is expected to erase. Remarkably, we find that the most ubiquitous noise -- random fluctuations of on-site energies (dephasing) -- instead renders this asymmetry topologically robust. The density profile develops a skewness that grows in time while its center stays fixed, and in a finite chain the late-time relaxation modes pile up at one edge: a skin effect lacking the drift of conventional non-Hermitian skin effects. With multiple sites per unit cell, the dephasing strength alone can cause a topological phase transition, reversing the asymmetry. On a flux ladder with noisy rung hopping, the noise causes a drift of rung coherences, a quantum ratchet with no classical counterpart. Underlying these effects, the noise-averaged dynamics is an interacting (generically non-integrable) Lindbladian that remains analytically tractable. The modes governing late-time relaxation are bound states of the noise-induced interaction and form a band with a point gap, absent both without noise and under postselection, whose winding number fixes the direction of the asymmetry. These effects are within reach of several experimental platforms, including synthetic lattices, superconducting qubits, and optical lattices.

papers.title: Dynamically Reentrant Skyrmion Phase in Oscillating Magnetic Fields
papers.abstract: We address a central open question in driven topological matter by investigating the nonequilibrium response of a two-dimensional magnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions subjected to a periodically oscillating magnetic field. Using extensive Monte Carlo simulations, we uncover a dynamically reentrant skyrmion phase that emerges within a finite window of field amplitudes and bias fields, sandwiched between the conventional skyrmion and polarized ferromagnetic phases. This phase has no equilibrium counterpart and originates from an imbalance between skyrmion creation and annihilation over a single field cycle, leading to a reversal of the period-averaged topological charge. We show that the re-entrant phase exists only in the dynamic response regime where the system can follow the drive, and is suppressed at higher driving frequencies. Our results establish periodic driving as a nonequilibrium control parameter for stabilizing and reversing skyrmion topology.

papers.title: Tunneling spectroscopy of topological insulator Josephson junctions
papers.abstract: In the seminal proposal by Fu and Kane, the superconducting proximity effect is used to realize topological superconductivity in the topological surface state (TSS) of a 3D topological insulator (TI). In a Josephson junction made on the TI surface, the spin-momentum locking of the TSS guarantees the existence of spin nondegenerate, perfectly transmitted Andreev modes. These modes lead to gap closing as a function of the superconducting phase difference $\varphi$. Here, we report the observation of highly transmissive Andreev modes in a TI Josephson junction, probed via tunnel contacts and $\varphi$ controlled by a flux loop. Within our experimental resolution, they could indicate a gap closing and reopening. This phenomenon is observed for a wide range of chemical potentials, supporting its TSS origin. Under an applied magnetic field, highly transmissive modes are observed locally, matching theoretical predictions for Josephson vortices in the TSS. Our results support the fundamental role of spin-momentum locking in the Andreev physics in the TSS.

papers.title: Helicons in multi-Weyl semimetals
papers.abstract: Helicons are low-frequency, circularly polarized transverse electromagnetic modes that propagate in three-dimensional conducting systems in the presence of a static magnetic field. Here, we investigate helicon excitations in gapless multi-Weyl semimetals (mWSMs) with topological charge \(J=1,2,\) and \(3\) using semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory. We incorporate both Berry-curvature and orbital-magnetic-moment corrections into the quasiparticle dynamics and determine the optical-conductivity tensor in the presence of a weak static magnetic field. The longitudinal conductivity is obtained analytically for single-, double and triple-Weyl systems, whereas the transverse conductivity is evaluated numerically in the low-frequency regime relevant to helicon propagation. We find that the cyclotron frequency acquires a nontrivial dependence on the topological charge and on the magnetic field. The resulting helicon dispersion retains the characteristic quadratic dependence on the wave vector, while the axion-electrodynamics contribution generates an additional linear term. We further show that the axion term lifts the degeneracy of the gapped collective modes at zero wave vector, with the resulting mode frequencies determined by the \(J\)-dependent plasma frequencies. These results demonstrate that the helicon response provides a probe of the distinct electrodynamic properties of multi-Weyl semimetals.

papers.title: Resonantly interacting $2e/3$ anyons: a controlled microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity
papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity that connects electronic interactions in a lightly doped Laughlin state to the universal physics of a resonantly interacting anyon gas. Using geometric quantization of Laughlin quasiholes, we derive the effective many-body Hamiltonian of dilute charge-$2e/3$ anyons, including their valley structure, dispersion, and statistical and short-range interactions, together with an explicit map between anyon and electron observables. This reduces the dilute many-body problem to a few parameters fixed by data computable from few anyon numerics. In analogy with resonant Fermi and Bose gases, we organize the dilute anyon problem around a two-body binding resonance and its relevant and marginal perturbations. For a three-valley gas of charge-$2e/3$ anyons, we identify a resonance whose long-distance theory is governed by an Aharonov-Casher anyon Hamiltonian whose magnetic field is the statistical Chern-Simons field and whose ground state is exactly solvable. Using the ground state wavefunction, we demonstrate Cooper-pair off-diagonal long-range order directly in electron coordinates and determine the pairing symmetry and vortex-lattice structure. The leading perturbations at the fixed point are a relevant pair detuning and a marginal three-body contact in the valley-singlet channel, which determine the compressibility and sound velocity. A repulsive three-body coupling is marginally irrelevant, allowing the fixed point to control a parametrically broad dilute regime near pair resonance, while attractive three-body interactions instead generate charge-$2e$ trimers. More broadly, our results show that binding thresholds between competing anyon composites host universal resonant regimes that are not captured by the lowest-energy anyon species alone, providing a new setting for controlled theories of anyon matter.

papers.title: Ni ordering in the van der Waals gap of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$: from disorder through $2\times2$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order to stripe order
papers.abstract: We report a synchrotron x-ray diffraction study of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$ over the range $0.18 \le x \le 0.57$, with Ni contents measured by energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy. Powder diffraction on the whole series shows that the NbS$_2$ host is preserved, while the Ni ions in the van der Waals gap evolve from a disordered arrangement to $2\times2$ order at $x=1/4$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order at $x=1/3$, through a range where both motifs coexist, to an orthorhombic stripe-type order at $x=0.57$. The in-plane lattice parameter increases with Ni content, whereas the interlayer spacing remains nearly constant except for a pronounced minimum at $x=1/4$, which density-functional calculations reproduce for the ordered structure. Single-crystal diffraction on the two commensurate phases shows that the $x=1/4$ structure, with Ni on a single site and a trimerized Nb lattice, is free of stacking faults, whereas the chiral $x=1/3$ structure contains Ni on the nominally empty site, inversion twins and stacking faults of the Ni layers. The comparison between powders and crystals shows that grinding mainly degrades the stacking of the Ni layers. These results establish the structural phase diagram of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ and the intercalant disorder to be taken into account in the interpretation of its magnetic properties.

papers.title: Interplay between Spin Stripes and Pairing Crossover in the Bilayer Hubbard Model
papers.abstract: Whether $d$-wave or $s_\pm$-wave pairing prevails in the bilayer nickelate \ce{La3Ni2O7} remains unresolved, and how its observed spin order and magnetic excitations relate to the pairing mechanism is unclear. Here, we use finite-temperature determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a minimal bilayer Hubbard model to investigate pairing competition at strong interlayer coupling, where intralayer and interlayer antiferromagnetic correlations have comparable strengths. We find that spin stripes develop spontaneously with increasing hole doping, accompanied by a crossover of the dominant pairing symmetry from $d$-wave to $s_\pm$-wave. The crossover tracks the changing relative strengths of the spin correlations, with the interlayer correlations overtaking their intralayer counterparts in magnitude. Concomitantly, the dynamical spin structure factor exhibits a momentum-dependent reorganization of the magnetic excitations, consistent with fluctuating spin stripes. Our results identify the structure of spin fluctuations as a key link between spin stripes and pairing competition, offering a minimal-model perspective for understanding \ce{La3Ni2O7}.

papers.title: Statistical mechanics and hierarchy of learnability in quantum codes: From generalized symmetries to non-Abelian topological orders
papers.abstract: Local weak measurements provide noisy information about observables encoded in a quantum code. We formulate the corresponding Bayesian inference problem for a broad class of topological stabilizer codes by mapping it to classical spin models with generalized symmetries. When the wavefunction deformation and Gaussian measurement strengths coincide, the replicated model acquires an enlarged symmetry. We use this symmetry to derive exact identities among correlators averaged over measurement records that quantify the learnability of nonlocal observables associated with fractionalized excitations. Together with correlation inequalities in the associated clean ferromagnetic models, these identities establish hierarchies of learnability: if two observables remain learnable at long distances, their product must also remain learnable. We demonstrate these relations in the rank-2 toric code and the X-cube model, whose classical descriptions exhibit modulated and subsystem symmetries, respectively. We further extend the analysis to finite group quantum double models, including non-Abelian ones. We derive exact relations between learnability and correlations in the corresponding classical models, and show that the representation structure and fusion rules of anyons impose further constraints under suitable positivity conditions. These results constrain which types of nonlocal information can be learned simultaneously, providing a guide to learning phase diagrams in quantum codes under local weak measurements.

papers.title: Field evolution of the multi-$k$ magnetic states in NdB$_4$ revealed by neutron diffraction
papers.abstract: We investigate the magnetic states of the Shastry-Sutherland-lattice magnet NdB$_4$ using single-crystal neutron diffraction. We focus on magnetic fields applied along the tetragonal $c$ axis, which stabilise the fractional 1/5~magnetisation plateau. In the low-temperature phase below 4.9 K, the transition into the plateau state at approximately 12 kOe is marked by a change in the propagation vectors from $(1/5,0,-2/5)$ and its double $(2/5,0,1/5)$ to $(0,0,1/5)$ and $(0,0,2/5)$. At the transition from the plateau to a nominally `field-polarised' state near 33 kOe, all magnetic reflections associated with non-integer propagation vectors disappear, whereas reflections corresponding to the $\mathbf{k}=0$ component persist throughout the entire field range. We conclude that that the in-plane components survive even in the high-field phase and that the polarisation is, in fact, incomplete. The observed field dependence provides direct support for a description of NdB$_4$ in terms of two coupled magnetic instabilities: all-in-all-out order of the in-plane moments and a spin-density wave of the out-of-plane components.

papers.title: Hidden entropic order of emergent charges in a classical Amp\`ere spin liquid
papers.abstract: Classical spin liquids are characterized by an extensive number of ground-state configurations. Coulomb spin liquids have, in this ground-state manifold, a divergence-free local constraint, which gives dipolar correlations and pinch points in the structure factor. Recently, models with a complementary ground-state constraint, defined by a zero-circulation constraint (Amp\`ere's law), have been proposed. While classical Coulomb spin liquids forbid emergent charges, their Amp\`ere counterparts leave the charges unconstrained. Here we study an Ising Amp\`ere model on the octochlore lattice. The ground states obey a Gauss law for an antisymmetric rank-two field, i.e., three coupled two-dimensional Gauss laws, which are expected to produce pinch points in the structure factor. Nevertheless, maximal charges, vertices with all six arrows in or out, spontaneously accumulate on one of the two sublattices of the cubic lattice, with disordered signs. This order has a purely entropic origin; it washes out the pinch-point singularities at large scales, produces no magnetic Bragg peaks, and coexists with an extensive entropy. The system enters into this sublattice long-range ordered state through a continuous transition in what seems to be the three-dimensional Ising universality class. Moreover, the state has no magnetic order; it is even under time reversal: it is a hidden, entropic order within the Amp\`ere manifold. Thus, a system whose Gauss law would predict an algebraic spin liquid becomes, through a non-magnetic ordering transition, a partially ordered short-range spin liquid. Our study is based on a combination of the constraint-vector theory, exact bounds and enumeration, and Monte Carlo, Wang-Landau, and parallel-tempering simulations.

papers.title: Simulating a chiral gauge theory
papers.abstract: Chiral gauge theories underlie the Standard Model, yet none has been simulated nonperturbatively. Lattice constructions that evade the Nielsen-Ninomiya obstruction entail complex fermion measures or infinite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces. Here we provide a gauge-invariant Hamiltonian lattice regularization of 1+1-dimensional abelian chiral gauge theories built from clock-and-shift qudits with $\mathbb{Z}_N$ gauge fields, in which the global chiral symmetry and its 't Hooft anomaly survive exactly mod $N$. Anomaly cancellation on the lattice lets the Gauss laws be imposed and solved exactly, reducing the theory to an unconstrained qudit chain. Using infinite matrix product states, we simulate the canonical 1+1-dimensional chiral gauge theory, the 34-50 model, and find excellent agreement with analytic predictions, showing that a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space at $N=6$ reproduces the expected infrared physics of the continuum 34-50 model. This provides an efficient and practical solution to the problem of simulating general abelian chiral gauge theories in 1+1 dimensions, both on classical and quantum computers.

papers.title: Charge Pumping Leptogenesis from the Symmetric Mass Generation Phase on a Four-Leg Ladder Lattice
papers.abstract: Quantized charge pumping in quantum Hall systems is a bulk topological property, typically manifesting on gapless boundaries as spectral flow through chiral edge modes upon flux insertion. When the boundary is anomaly-free, it can be symmetrically gapped by symmetric mass generation (SMG) interactions. However, the effects on quantized charge pumping at an interacting gapped boundary are unclear. We address this using density-matrix renormalization group simulations of a four-leg ladder quasi-(2+1)d realization of the (1+1)d 3-4-5-0 lattice chiral fermion model with six-fermion interactions at one edge. We find gapless modes near the interacting edge for both weak and strong couplings, but the edge can be in a fully gapped SMG phase at intermediate coupling. We also identify spontaneous breaking of the model's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry above a critical interaction strength. Across all three boundary phases, we find quantized charge pumping with the same pumped charge per flux quantum. The spatial distribution of the pumped charge varies between phases. Besides charge pumping, we study how a single injected fermion propagates under open boundary conditions. In the SMG phase, an interaction-induced flavor-mixing current develops at the endpoints of the gapped edge, which is absent in the weak- and strong-coupling limits. This current reveals a charge-redistribution mechanism unique to the SMG phase. Additionally, we propose an analogy between charge pumping in this model and a topological leptogenesis scenario in the (3+1)d Standard Model. The anomaly-free chiral U(1) symmetries of the 3-4-5-0 model play a role analogous to the baryon-minus-lepton symmetry of the Standard Model. In both settings, charge pumping can be associated with a continuous deformation along a classically defined but quantum-anomalous direction, while a discrete subgroup remains an exact quantum symmetry.

papers.title: Rotated-Frame Determinant Discovery for Ground- and Excited-State Quantum Selected Configuration Interaction
papers.abstract: Quantum Selected Configuration Interaction (QSCI) constructs a variational determinant space from measurements of a prepared electronic state, but finite-shot sampling can repeatedly observe high-probability determinants, limiting efficient discovery of configurations important for an accurate selected-CI description. We introduce rotate--sample--unrotate (RSU) determinant discovery, in which the same state is sampled in complementary orbital frames and the observed rotated determinants generate a finite set of candidates in the canonical basis. The Hamiltonian is then diagonalized in an orthonormal selected-CI space without enumerating the full determinant space. State-targeted orbital frames are constructed from an initial selected-CI wavefunction and its external residual. For excited states, we combine RSU with the generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) to prepare target-specific sampling states. Candidate GQE circuits are evaluated by classical selected-CI diagonalization in finite sampled spaces, so the quantum procedure requires only state preparation and determinant sampling. For N$_2$, exact-state controls isolate the determinant-discovery effect: at the stretched geometry, residual-natural-orbital RSU reaches chemical accuracy with 5,000 shots, compared with 20,000 shots for conventional QSCI. The improvement persists with approximate GQE-prepared states and is also observed for target excited states. These results demonstrate improved finite-shot determinant discovery in QSCI for both ground and excited states.

papers.title: Spatial Cost of Recovering a Fusion Qubit in a Critical Spin Chain
papers.abstract: Vanishing-error recovery of a fusion qubit from a fixed-sector ground doublet of four Kramers--Wannier defects in a critical Ising chain requires at least the shorter three-defect span of physical spins to leading order. Across arbitrary preselected spin sets and unrestricted joint decoding, this bound holds when the thermodynamic limit precedes large spacings at fixed positive ratios. An exact interval decoder attains it. Collective records of both logical axes in the complement force successful near-minimal supports to concentrate in density on a leading-order shortest interval.

papers.title: Tree tensor network states represent low-energy states faithfully
papers.abstract: Extending corresponding results for matrix product states [Verstraete and Cirac, PRB 73, 094423 (2006); Schuch et al. PRL 100, 030504 (2008)], it is shown how the approximation error of tree tensor network states (TTNS) can be bounded using Schmidt spectra or R\'{e}nyi entanglement entropies of the target quantum state. Conversely, one obtains bounds on TTNS bond dimensions needed to achieve a specific approximation accuracy. The result implies that efficient TTNS approximations exist if $\alpha<1$ R\'{e}nyi entanglement entropies for single-branch cuts obey an area law, as in ground and low-energy states of certain gapped systems on tree graphs.

papers.title: Cost scaling of MPS and TTNS simulations for 2D and 3D systems with area-law entanglement
papers.abstract: Tensor network states are an indispensable tool for the simulation of strongly correlated quantum many-body systems. In recent years, tree tensor network states (TTNS) have been successfully used for two-dimensional systems and to benchmark quantum simulation approaches for condensed matter, nuclear, and particle physics. In comparison to the more traditional approach based on matrix product states (MPS), the graph distance of physical degrees of freedom can be drastically reduced in TTNS. Surprisingly, it turns out that, for large systems in $D>1$ spatial dimensions, MPS simulations of low-energy states are nevertheless more efficient than TTNS simulations. With a focus on $D=2$ and 3, the scaling of computational costs for different boundary conditions is determined under the assumption that the system obeys an entanglement (log-)area law, implying that bond dimensions scale exponentially in the interface area of the associated subsystems.

papers.title: Entropic Barriers and the Kinetic Suppression of Topological Defects
papers.abstract: Many quantum phases, from topological orders to superfluids, are destabilized at finite temperature by the proliferation and motion of topological defects such as anyons or vortices. Conventional protection mechanisms rely on energetic gaps and fail once thermal fluctuations exceed the gap scale. Here we examine a complementary mechanism of entropic protection, in which defect nucleation is suppressed by coupling to mesoscopic auxiliary reservoirs of dimension $M$, generating an effective free-energy barrier that increases with temperature. In the Ising chain, this produces a characteristic three-regime evolution of the correlation length as a function of temperature - linear growth, entropy-controlled plateau, and eventual breakdown - indicating a general modification of defect behavior. Focusing on two spatial dimensions, where true finite-temperature topological order is forbidden in the thermodynamic limit, we show that entropic protection can nevertheless strongly enhance stabilization at finite system size, the regime directly relevant for quantum memory and experiments. Owing to the topological character of the defects, creation and transport are independently suppressed, yielding a double parametric reduction of logical errors in the entropic toric code and enhanced coherence when the framework is extended to Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions. Entropic barriers thus provide a passive and scalable route to stabilizing quantum phases in experimentally relevant regimes. We propose an experimental setup for entropic toric code using dual species Rydberg arrays with dressing.

papers.title: Toric codes all the way down: decoupling translation-invariant topological CSS codes in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: Topological Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes in more than two spatial dimensions offer features useful for fault-tolerant quantum computation, such as transversal non-Clifford gates and single-shot decoding, but a systematic understanding of them is still lacking. One approach is to decouple a code: map it to a stack of higher-form toric codes by a finite-depth local CSS-preserving Clifford circuit, possibly after adding ancillas. For translation-invariant $p$-ary CSS codes, where $p$ is prime ($p=2$ for qubits), we require the circuit to commute with the translations of a superlattice. In two dimensions, such a decoupling exists once these translations act trivially on every anyon type. In higher dimensions, excitations are sorted by their dimension into superselection layers, which can remain glued together even when translations act trivially on each layer. We show that this gluing is the only remaining obstruction: a code can be decoupled on a superlattice exactly when, after coarse-graining to it, translations act trivially on every layer and the gluing vanishes. Moreover, for a code with finitely many excitation types in each layer and $m$ nonzero layers, once translations act trivially on every layer, further coarse-graining by a factor of $p^{m-1}$ in every direction removes the aforementioned gluing. Physically, the same criterion determines when the code encodes the maximal number of logical qudits on a finite torus. Finally, we give an explicit algorithm that constructs the decoupling as a circuit of SUM (qudit CNOT) and SWAP gates.

papers.title: LaQX: A JAX Toolkit for Neural Quantum State Simulations of Lattice Quantum Many-Body Models
papers.abstract: Neural quantum states provide accurate variational representations for interacting lattice fermions and spins. Turning a new ansatz into a reproducible calculation, however, requires coordinated implementations of the Hamiltonian, sampling, optimization, observables, and accelerator parallelism. We present LaQX (Lattice Quantum simulation based on jaX), an open-source neural quantum state library based on JAX that organizes these components through common functional interfaces. Beyond ground-state variational Monte Carlo, LaQX supports excited-state calculations, Green's Function Monte Carlo refinement, adiabatic evolution, and real-time evolution with time-dependent variational Monte Carlo. It consolidates methods developed in recent high-accuracy neural quantum state studies of the Hubbard model and frustrated magnets, and the package has been used to investigate the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model. We document these capabilities with reproducible calculations for Hubbard, $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg, altermagnetic Hubbard, and interacting Hofstadter models. Function-oriented modules separate the scientific components and limit the source context needed for extensions by human developers and large language models. Source code, documentation, and executable examples are available at https://github.com/bytedance/laqx.

papers.title: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits
papers.abstract: We prove that the three-dimensional chiral $\Z_p$ Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun--Yang--Wang--Tantivasadakarn--Chen are, for every odd prime $p$, not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.

papers.title: On flat band engineering and graphene nanomesh magnonics
papers.abstract: Graph-theoretic topological frustration is a peculiar situation on a finite piece of the honeycomb lattice that prevents a full pairwise coupling of the lattice sites via nearest neighbor links, even when the total number of sites is an even number and the structure possesses no sublattice imbalance. This type of frustration is inherent for organic molecules that are classified as concealed non-Kekulean hydrocarbons, representing peculiar diradicals. Here we show that this topological frustration persists in two-dimensional systems based on the honeycomb lattice. Such systems exhibit fully flat electronic energy bands located at the Fermi level. Therefore, two-dimensional ultimately flat bands can be systematically and predictably constructed for graphene monolayer nanomeshes. These systems are prone to antiferromagnetic ordering and hybrid spin-wave excitations mixing weak ferromagnetic and strong antiferromagnetic features, which could pave the way towards low-power, compact, and ultrafast organic spintronics with near room-temperature operation.

papers.title: Finite-size scaling theory of R\'enyi thermal entropy for second-order, first-order, and weakly first-order quantum phase transitions
papers.abstract: Establishing the nature of a quantum phase transition in finite-size simulations---whether continuous, first-order, or weakly first-order---is a fundamental challenge in quantum many-body computation. The weakly first-order transition is particularly elusive: its anomalously large correlation length invariably mimics a continuous critical point at accessible system sizes, and no unified finite-size scaling theory has existed to distinguish these scenarios under realistic computational constraints. In this work, we address this problem by introducing a finite-size scaling framework based on the R\'enyi thermal entropy (RTE) and its derivative (DRTE). We derive the finite-size scaling forms for the RTE and DRTE at continuous, first-order, and weakly first-order quantum phase transitions, and show that the DRTE isolates the universal contribution of the free energy and strengthens the characteristics of various phase transitions in finite sizes. Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate accurate data collapse and extraction of critical exponents at (2+1)-dimensional O($N$) critical points. Most importantly, the DRTE provides a definitive signature of weakly first-order transitions at visitable sizes---a zero-crossing and a double-peak structure---which we observe in the debated deconfined quantum criticality candidates such as the $J$--$Q$ and SU(8) $J_1$--$J_2$ models. Our approach offers a general, order-parameter-agnostic, and numerically efficient diagnostic tool, resolving long-standing ambiguities between continuous and weakly first-order scenarios in the finite size simulations.

papers.title: On the near-horizon interpretation of Krylov dynamics
papers.abstract: The Lanczos recursion maps operator growth onto the motion of a wave function on a semi-infinite chain, and for linearly growing Lanczos coefficients the deep region of the chain behaves like the near-horizon region of a black hole. We develop this correspondence in the time domain and determine how far it extends. Writing the Krylov equation as an exactly skew-adjoint difference operator, we derive a unitary continuum limit whose corrections are suppressed by $n^{-2}$ once the origin of the chain is fixed by the offset of the Lanczos coefficients. For $b_n\simeq\alpha n$ the Krylov evolution is chiral transport in $\ln n$, which coincides with infalling waves near the horizon of an AdS$_2$ black hole when the Krylov depth is identified with the blueshift of an infalling particle; this fixes $\alpha=\pi T$, while staggered configurations of the chain carry the outgoing chirality. For $b_n=\alpha\sqrt{n(n+2h-1)}$ the correspondence is exact: the Krylov basis is the discrete series of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ carried by a bulk scalar of mass $m^2L^2=h(h-1)$, the Liouvillian is the boost generator of the black hole at temperature $T=\alpha/\pi$, and positivity of $b_n^2$ reproduces the Breitenlohner--Freedman bound, saturated by strictly linear coefficients. Beyond leading order we prove that, for every Lanczos sequence with a smooth large-$n$ expansion, the ingoing solutions of the Krylov equation have coefficients polynomial in frequency to all orders in $1/n$, whereas a massive bulk field has a pole at the first special point $\omega=-2\pi iT$ with residue proportional to $m^2$. Smooth subleading Lanczos data therefore cannot encode the bulk mass locally. The obstruction persists for the BTZ black hole, for which we obtain the Lanczos coefficients in closed form.

papers.title: Successive single- and double-q $\Gamma_3$ quadrupole orders on the diamond structure
papers.abstract: We investigate field-dependent quadrupolar ordering at the L points of the diamond-structure Brillouin zone using classical Monte Carlo simulations of an effective $\Gamma_3$ quadrupole model. We demonstrate that competition between the magnetic field and quadrupole anisotropy leads to a rich phase diagram for magnetic fields applied parallel to [001], which includes switching between a single-q state and a double-q state. We also examine the effects of a symmetry-allowed biquadratic intersite interaction, corresponding to a hexadecapole interaction, on the stability of the double-q state under a magnetic field.

papers.title: The multichannel Dyson equation for double ionisation spectroscopies
papers.abstract: Several photoemission spectroscopies and, in particular, Auger spectroscopy, involve double-ionization processes. For the numerical simulation of these spectroscopies it is convenient to use the particle-particle channel of the two-body Green's functions since its poles correspond to excitation energies in which the final state has two more particles (holes or electrons) than the initial state. In standard approaches it is approximated within the random phase approximation. As a consequence only the quasiparticles of the photoemission spectrum are captured but none of the satellites features. In this work, we go beyond this approximation by employing the multichannel Dyson equation. By coupling the particle-particle two-body Green's function to the 3-hole-1-electron and 3-electron-1-hole channels of the four-body Green's function, the multichannel Dyson equation incorporates correlations beyond the RPA in a straightforward way. We are thus able to describe both quasiparticles and satellites in the photoemission spectra.

papers.title: Hidden weak-pairing superconductivity of non-interacting anyons obeying 1/3 statistics
papers.abstract: We show that a non-interacting gas of charge-$e/3$ anyons with exchange statistics $\theta=-\pi/3$ can superconduct through a hidden weak-pairing mechanism. Such an anyon gas arises naturally in doped fractional Chern insulators at filling $1/3$ or $2/3$, where projective lattice translations enforce three degenerate anyon pockets. Exploiting this three-pocket structure, we develop a flux-attachment construction in which the average statistical flux vanishes, thereby mapping the problem to three species of composite fermions (CFs) in zero effective magnetic field. We show that the anyon statistics itself, encoded in statistical gauge field fluctuations, supplies the pairing glue and drives the CFs into a $p-\mathrm{i}p$ paired state, which corresponds to a $f-\mathrm{i}f$ physical superconductor. The CF strong-pairing phase is adiabatically connected to Laughlin's picture of anyon superconductivity, where charge-$e/3$ anyons bind into charge-$2e/3$ molecules, which then lead to superconductivity. By contrast, the more natural weak-pairing phase of CFs realizes a distinct superconducting phase - its edge is characterized by a chiral central charge $c_-=-1/2$, in contrast to the prediction of integer $c_-$ for the anyon superconductor based on Laughlin's picture, thereby resolving the discrepancy between previous theories and recent numerical results. Our theory provides a natural framework for understanding superconductivity near fractional Chern insulators, as observed in recent experiments. Finally, we discuss extensions of our theory that predict new chiral superconductors adjacent to FCIs at other fillings.

papers.title: Complexity of tensor network simulation for noisy quantum circuits
papers.abstract: We aim to rigorously address how local noise affects the classical simulability of quantum dynamics benchmarked by tensor-network methods. Using operator entanglement entropy (OEE) as a unifying criterion, we prove the following: (1) For single-qubit depolarizing noise, geometry-independent $\order{1}$-layer and $\Theta(\log n)$-layer thresholds for fixed absolute and relative Hilbert--Schmidt error are established, beyond which polynomial bond dimension suffices; on 1D local circuits with a product initial input, whole-trajectory MPO approximations are constructed at fixed purified distance with $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ bond dimension. (2) For general single-qubit noise, we identify sufficient contractivity conditions for MPO approximations with constant bond dimension, in both the average and worst cases. (3) We further extend the above results to higher dimensions, yielding $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ average boundary-bond dimensions for projected entangled pair operators (PEPO) across every cut. Our results establish a rigorous connection between certain noise models, circuit types, and their classical simulability.
